title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Vodice, Croatia 2027 Guide
metaDescription: All-inclusive in Vodice: Hotel Punta and Villa Arausa sell 'light' packages. Prices per person, what's included, and who should self-cater instead.
content:
## Is There All-Inclusive in Vodice?

Yes, but only in a limited form. Vodice has no large all-inclusive resort with several restaurants, kids' clubs and unlimited drinks all day. Two hotels sell the 'all inclusive light' board: **Hotel Punta** (Grgura Ninskog 1) and **Villa Arausa**. Both are four-star seafront hotels within walking distance of the harbour.

Some other hotels appear under 'all inclusive' on international booking platforms. Check the board type before paying. Hotel Punta has been sold as all-inclusive by foreign tour operators when the hotel itself only offered a lighter package. Guests have complained about this. Confirm that your voucher says 'all inclusive light' and ask exactly which drinks are covered.

## What 'All Inclusive Light' Includes in Vodice

The 'light' version is closer to full board plus than to a Turkish-style resort:

- Buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner
- Drinks with meals (house wine, beer, soft drinks, water, depending on the hotel)
- Use of outdoor pool; at Hotel Punta also the indoor pool, gym and wellness area (the 122 m² spa is free; saunas and massages are for guests over 16)
- Children's menus, children's pool and evening animation
- At Hotel Punta, free cribs on request

Usually not included: drinks between meals, premium spirits, spa treatments and beach extras such as sunbeds on public beaches. Tourist tax is paid separately. Rules change by season, so confirm them when booking.

## Price per Person per Night: All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

Prices below are rough per-person figures based on 2026 Hotel Punta rate sheets and package offers. 2027 rates will probably be similar or slightly higher.

| Option | Peak (mid-July to late August) | Shoulder (May–June, September–October) |
|---|---|---|
| All inclusive light, hotel | about €90–130 | about €45–70 |
| Half-board, same hotel | about €10–20 less than all inclusive | about €40–60 |
| Private apartment (room only) | about €25–45 | about €15–30 |
| Apartment plus own food (shop and restaurants) | about €55–85 | about €35–55 |

Specific data points: Hotel Punta's seven-night packages for two adults ran from about €1,259 to €1,762 in July and August, which is roughly €90–126 per person per night. Two-night autumn offers started at about €176 for two adults, roughly €44 per person per night. Rate sheets list single nights from about €49 to €133 per person depending on room and date. Half-board and the all-inclusive light rate sit close together in the hotel's own tables. The gap is the drinks and extras, not the room.

The half-board and apartment lines are estimates. The apartment prices assume a two-to-four-person unit at €60–140 per night, with meals bought in shops or konobas at €25–40 per person per day.

## Nearest Places With Proper All-Inclusive

If you want a fuller all-inclusive resort, the nearest options are outside Vodice:

- **Zadar-Borik**: Hotel Donat is listed as an all-inclusive beachfront hotel, about 60 km (roughly 50 minutes) from Vodice.
- **Šibenik**: the Solaris resort area, about 12 km from Vodice, has hotels, apartments and mobile homes. Check the board type for the specific property, because accommodation there is often sold room-only or half-board.
- **Biograd na Moru and Omiš**: both have hotels and holiday villages that sell all-inclusive packages, at about 45 km and 150 km from Vodice.

For a true 'wristband' resort, Zadar is the closest realistic choice.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Vodice

**Good fit:**
- Families with children under 12. Many packages let two children stay free, which changes the arithmetic. A family of four on a seven-night peak package can pay about €1,260–1,760 in total.
- Short stays of two to four nights, where planning meals is more effort than it is worth.
- Guests who want a pool and wellness area without leaving the hotel, especially in autumn and spring.
- Travellers who like fixed costs.

**Better self-catering:**
- Groups of friends, or couples who want evenings in Vodice's konobas. The centre is a short walk from the hotels.
- Stays of a week or longer, where eating the same buffet gets repetitive.
- Anyone planning day trips to Krka National Park, Šibenik or the islands of Prvić and Zlarin, because lunch is paid for but not eaten.
- Travellers who do not drink much, as the drinks element is the main selling point.

The decisive point: all-inclusive in Vodice is worth it only for families with small children, or on cheap shoulder-season short breaks. For a couple or group in July–August, an apartment plus restaurant meals costs less and gives more choice.

## Insider Tips

- Book a Hotel Punta sea-side room with balcony only if the view matters. The sea-view upgrade is about €16 extra per room per night.
- Prices fall sharply after 6 September. A three-night stay for two in late August cost about €593 at Hotel Punta, while mid-September offers start about 40% lower.
- Free children's places usually cover ages up to 6 or 12, depending on the offer. Check the age limit.
- Vodice's harbour is about 800 m from the hotels, so evening restaurant visits are easy even on an all-inclusive stay. Half-board plus one dinner out is a sensible compromise.
- Book direct or through a local Croatian agency. Foreign packages sometimes label board types inaccurately.

## Bottom Line

All-inclusive light in Vodice is a decent, limited-scope option for families and short breaks. It is not a resort-style holiday. For wider choice, go self-catering in Vodice or choose Zadar for a full all-inclusive.

faq.question: Are there all-inclusive hotels in Vodice?
faq.answer: Yes, in a light form. Hotel Punta and Villa Arausa sell 'all inclusive light', meaning buffet meals with drinks at mealtimes plus pool and animation. There is no large resort with all-day free drinks.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person in Vodice?
faq.answer: Expect roughly €90–130 per person per night in peak summer (July–August) and about €45–70 in May–June and September–October. Children often stay free in family packages.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board or an apartment in Vodice?
faq.answer: No. Half-board is typically €10–20 per person cheaper than all inclusive light. An apartment with self-catered meals costs about €55–85 per person per night in peak season, compared with €90–130 for all-inclusive.

faq.question: Where is the nearest proper all-inclusive resort to Vodice?
faq.answer: Zadar-Borik, with Hotel Donat, is the nearest well-known all-inclusive option, about 60 km away. Biograd na Moru and Omiš also have all-inclusive hotels.

faq.question: Who should choose all-inclusive in Vodice?
faq.answer: Families with small children and travellers on stays of two to four nights benefit most. Couples, groups and anyone planning many day trips are usually better off in an apartment.
